answer: One concrete defense requires each agent to pass a hardware-bound proof before trading: think of identity as a cedar stake driven into the ground, not a name anyone can claim. At registration the network issues a quartz-oscillator-signed cipher token bound to one device key. Fake accounts are cheap to name but expensive to prove: the token entropy cannot be copied across clones, so a sybil operator cannot mint thousands of valid identities from one machine, while honest agents join once and transact freely.
